record.paper_title: Four nucleon systems: a zoom to the open problems in nuclear interaction
record.original_question: Are nucleon-nucleon P-wave interactions, especially neutron-neutron P-waves and their charge dependence, incorrectly constrained in current nuclear interaction models, and can a physically acceptable P-wave correction explain the neutron plus tritium resonance-region disagreement and related failures in neutron-rich or P-wave-sensitive observables? The motivation is that neutron-neutron P-waves are not directly controlled by experiment, that a roughly 20% change in the neutron-neutron P-wave potential would be needed for AV18 to describe the resonance cross sections, and that discrepancies in helium-isotope binding energies grow with neutron excess even when three-nucleon forces improve the overall agreement.

evidence.quote: On contrary rare physical observables, where NN P-waves are important, have tendency to disagree with the experimental data. One such example could be the 3N analyzing powers [17, 18]. Higher NN waves should contribute in asymmetric nuclear systems; n+3H system due to its large neutron excess is one such case.
The discrepancy increases linearly with neutron excess, even if 3NF improves overall agreement it does not remove this tendency.

All these statements speaks against good description of NN interaction in P-waves. One should also recall that NN interaction is basically tuned on n-p and p-p data. Moreover, low energy p-p P-waves are overcasted by Coulomb repulsion, while n-n P-waves are not directly controlled by experiment at all.

We have evaluated, see Fig. 3, how much n-n P-wave potential must be changed in order to describe resonance cross sections for Av18 model. It turns to be of order ∼ 20%, which is rather much to blame on charge dependence in P-waves as well as compared to ∼ 6-8% necessary to solve Ay puzzle in n-d scattering [17, 18].
Still this study suggests that charge dependence effects can be sizeable in n-n P-waves and can provide a possible explanation for the disagreement observed in n-3H resonance region.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the standard framework of low-energy nuclear physics in which two nucleons (proton p and neutron n) interact via a charge-dependent nucleon-nucleon (NN) potential decomposed into partial waves, supplemented when needed by a three-nucleon force (3NF). A widely used realistic potential of this kind (e.g. of the AV18 type) is fit primarily to proton-proton (pp) and neutron-proton (np) scattering data plus the deuteron, with charge-symmetry/charge-independence breaking used to infer neutron-neutron (nn) partial waves. Because no direct free nn scattering experiments exist, the nn P-wave components are not directly constrained by data; meanwhile pp P-waves at low energy are masked by the Coulomb repulsion.

Investigate the following questions:

(a) Are the NN P-wave interactions in current realistic NN potentials — in particular the nn ¹P₁, ³P₀, ³P₁, ³P₂ components and their charge dependence relative to pp and np — incorrectly constrained, in the sense that the present treatment of charge dependence in P-waves is insufficient to reproduce P-wave-sensitive observables in light nuclei?

(b) Does there exist a physically acceptable modification of the nn P-wave potential (i.e. a modification consistent with all directly measured NN data, with charge-symmetry-breaking expectations, and with deuteron and few-body bound-state properties) that simultaneously
 (i) brings calculations of the n + ³H elastic cross section in the resonance region into agreement with measurement,
 (ii) accounts for the systematic, approximately linear growth with neutron excess of the discrepancy between computed and measured helium-isotope binding energies that persists after inclusion of standard 3NFs, and
 (iii) is compatible with (or helps resolve) the nucleon-deuteron vector analyzing-power (Aᵧ) puzzle?

Quantitatively, determine whether a change of order 20% in the nn P-wave potential strength needed to reproduce the n + ³H resonance cross section with an AV18-type interaction is admissible as genuine charge dependence in the P-waves (noting that only of order 6–8% modification of NN P-waves is typically associated with the Aᵧ puzzle), or whether such a large modification must instead be attributed to missing many-nucleon dynamics.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches indicate the Aᵧ puzzle and discrepancies in P-wave-sensitive few-nucleon observables remain unresolved. Progress with chiral N²LO three-nucleon forces and optimized chiral interactions has reduced but not eliminated the Aᵧ discrepancy, and no consensus exists on whether modifying nn P-waves (in particular as charge-dependence effects) suffices to remove the n + ³H resonance disagreement and the linear growth of helium-isotope binding-energy errors with neutron excess. The status is therefore best characterized as open.

status_evidence.title: The Ay puzzle and the nuclear force
status_evidence.snippet: It is not possible with reasonable changes in the NN potential to increase the three-body Ay and at the same time keep the two-body observables unchanged; the Ay puzzle is likely to be solved by new three-nucleon forces.
status_evidence.claim: The nucleon-deuteron Aᵧ puzzle, closely linked to NN P-wave uncertainties, remains an unresolved problem.

status_evidence.title: Low-energy P–D elastic scattering and the "Ay puzzle"
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of persistent disagreement between calculations and measured Ay in low-energy nucleon-deuteron scattering.
status_evidence.claim: The P-wave-sensitive Aᵧ discrepancy in low-energy three-nucleon scattering is documented as ongoing.

status_evidence.title: Nucleon-deuteron scattering and the puzzle to N3LO
status_evidence.snippet: Calculations at N3LO in chiral EFT still show partial discrepancies with measured analyzing powers.
status_evidence.claim: Even state-of-the-art chiral NN+3N calculations have not fully resolved P-wave-sensitive few-nucleon discrepancies.
